skill.name: agentic-workflow
skill.description: Practical workflows for AI coding agents that cover command references, session handling, Git worktrees, MCP coordination, and containerized experimentation.
skill.summary: Coordinate AI coding agents with practical command, Git, MCP, and session workflows.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily instructional Markdown, and most static hits are false positives from command names, shortcuts, and fenced examples. The unsafe container setup is confirmed because it pipes a remote installer into sh and forwards ANTHROPIC_API_KEY into a container with a workspace mount. No prompt injection or hidden malicious prose was found.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to shell in the Dockerfile example.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell with a pinned package, checksum verification, or separate download and signature verification steps.

remediation.issue: API key is forwarded into a general-purpose container.
remediation.suggestion: Use short-lived tokens, least-privilege scopes, and avoid passing secrets unless the image and commands are trusted.

remediation.issue: The container command mounts the current workspace into the container.
remediation.suggestion: Use an explicit path, prefer read-only mounts where possible, and avoid mounting secrets or unrelated files.

remediation.issue: Workflow examples encourage broad shell command execution.
remediation.suggestion: Add review gates that require users to inspect command intent before executing Git, Docker, or MCP shell commands.

static_findings.snippet: | `/init` | Auto-generate a CLAUDE.md draft | Start a new project |
| `/usage` | Show token usage/reset time | Start of every session |
| `/clear` | Clear conversation history | When context is polluted; start a new task |
| `/context` | Context window X-Ray | When performance degrades |
| `/clone` | Clone the entire conversation | A/B experiments; backups |
| `!cmd` | Run immediately without Claude processing | Quick status checks |
| `Esc Esc` | Cancel the last task immediately | Highest |

content.value_statement: Teams lose time when AI coding sessions, Git work, and tool usage are managed inconsistently. This skill provides concise workflows for sessions, shortcuts, Git reviews, MCP usage, and multi-agent task coordination.
actual_capabilities: Lists common Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex CLI commands.
Summarizes useful Claude Code keyboard shortcuts for session control.
Describes Git workflows for commits, pull requests, worktrees, and reviews.
Explains MCP server use for browser testing, databases, crawling, and large-codebase analysis.
Shows multi-agent patterns that divide planning, analysis, coding, testing, and reporting.
Provides container and troubleshooting examples for isolated experiments and context management.
limitations: It is a workflow guide, not an automation script.
It does not verify command safety before a user runs an example.
Some Docker guidance uses risky installation and secret-forwarding patterns.
It assumes users already understand their local CLI and repository permissions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Daily Sessions
use_cases.description: Use concise commands, shortcuts, and recovery steps to keep AI coding sessions focused.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Pull Request Work
use_cases.description: Define shared AI-assisted workflows for commits, draft pull requests, and review prompts.

use_cases.title: Plan Tooling for Large Tasks
use_cases.description: Select MCP, container, and multi-agent patterns for testing and broad codebase analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Guided Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agentic-workflow skill to set up a focused AI coding session for this repository. Include session naming, context checks, and safe first commands.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Git Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agentic-workflow skill to review my current changes, propose a commit message, and outline a draft pull request summary without committing yet.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate MCP Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agentic-workflow skill to choose MCP tools for browser testing, database inspection, and large-codebase analysis. Explain which tools are needed and why.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Multi-Agent Delivery Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agentic-workflow skill to design a multi-agent workflow for API design, implementation, tests, and final reporting. Include handoff points and verification steps.

output_examples.input: I need to start a clean Claude Code session for a bug fix.
output_examples.output: A concise checklist covering token usage, context cleanup, session naming, and first repository inspection steps.

output_examples.input: I want an AI-assisted pull request review workflow.
output_examples.output: A review sequence that checks out the pull request, summarizes changes, inspects risky files, asks for improvements, and runs verification.

output_examples.input: I need to divide a feature across Claude, Gemini, and Codex.
output_examples.output: A role plan where Claude designs and implements, Gemini analyzes broad context, Codex runs tests, and Claude synthesizes results.

best_practices: Confirm every shell, Docker, and Git command before running it.
Use separate worktrees for unrelated changes to keep AI sessions focused.
Limit MCP servers to the tools needed for the current task.
anti_patterns: Running copied install commands without checking their source or integrity.
Passing long-lived API keys into containers or shared shell sessions.
Using one overloaded AI context for unrelated workstreams.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and command examples. The user or agent still decides what to run.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It references Claude, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Git, Docker, and MCP servers.

faq.question: Is it suitable for new users?
faq.answer: Yes. New users should review each command and start with session and shortcut guidance.

faq.question: Can it help with pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflows for commit messages, draft pull requests, and review prompts.

faq.question: Does it require MCP servers?
faq.answer: No. MCP guidance is optional and useful for browser, database, crawling, and large-context tasks.

faq.question: What safety checks are important?
faq.answer: Inspect shell and Docker examples, avoid unverified installers, and keep API keys scoped and temporary.
